newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sues New York City over water supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sues New York City over water supply.

text.p: The federal government Thursday sued New York City for failing to filter drinking water from a watershed that provides 10 percent of the city's supply.

The Justice Department said drinking water from the Croton water supply, located just north of the city, did not pose an immediate health threat, but said filtration was needed to assure the safety of the water supply.
The federal Safe Drinking Water Act required that all surface water systems, such as Croton, filter water by June 1993, unless strict measures were met to make filtration unnecessary.
New York City disinfects Croton water before distribution, but the Justice Department said that is not enough to eliminate all disease-causing organisms.
Filtering reduces risks of waterborne diseases in surface water systems, which may be tainted by human and animal wastes and by microbes such as cryptosporidium.

Federal officials told the city in January that they intended to sue and began negotiations. The Justice Department said it will continue to try to reach a settlement that gives the city enough time to finish a study of potential sites for the filtration plant.

Under the Safe Drinking Water law, the city could have applied for a filtration waiver for the Croton system if it had demonstrated exceptional water quality and showed the quality could be protected.
But federal officials said the city did not apply for the waiver, and the Environmental Protection Agency determined that filtration was needed to protect public health.
